brief: A small-parts organizer with at least six separate bins.

requirements.evidence: A compact cluster of six cells with half-depth bins that suit small parts. In the staging, each bin holds screws, nuts, standoffs or small tools.
Six separate half-depth bins (stem hex-bin-half), one in each of cells 0,0,0, 1,0,0, 2,0,0, 0,1,0, 1,1,0 and -1,1,0.

finish.summary:
I built a small-parts organizer with six separate bins. It has six full hex bases in a compact two-row cluster (2,0,0 / 1,0,0 / 0,0,0 on one row and 1,1,0 / 0,1,0 / -1,1,0 on the other). Each base holds its own half-depth drop-in bin. I capped the open outer faces with 18 solid end caps and bolted the joints together with 9 joint bolts, for 30 parts in total. The configurator estimates about 2.65 kg of filament and roughly 62 hours of printing.

To show what it's for, I put M3 screws, nuts, standoffs, a solder reel, electrical tape and tweezers in the bins, one item per bin. These sit below the bin rims, so they're hard to see from the side but visible from above. The build check found no rule problems and no part collisions.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
